title: Lumen Telecom - Eval Playbook & Prompt Suite
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document is the customer-specific evaluation playbook for Lumen Telecom's language-model powered ticket summarization and routing feature. It consolidates pinned prompts, private dataset notes, acceptance criteria, regression checks, and the sign-off checklist required for model onboarding into Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments.

Intended audience:
Applied ML engineers, solutions engineering, SRE, security/compliance reviewers, Lumen product stakeholders.

High-level goals:
- Validate functional correctness on Lumen ticket and CRM data (summary fidelity, extraction accuracy).
- Ensure no PII leakage from private datasets and KMS/HSM flows are intact.
- Meet latency/cost targets for Dedicated capacity.
- Establish regression tests for prompt/drift detection and a clear sign-off path.

Customer context and constraints:
- Lumen provides three private datasets (support_tickets_2019_2023, escalation_logs_Q1_2024, agent_notes_anon_v2). Data is stored in a private S3 bucket accessible by Redwood Private through the customer's VPC peering.
- Allowed PII handling: only tokenized IDs may be returned; raw phone numbers and SSNs must be redacted. Redaction is enforced by an L7 pre-filter lambda before requests reach the model.
- SLA target for 95th percentile latency: 450ms for single-turn summarization on Dedicated with 512-token windows.

Pinned prompt suite (canonical set used for acceptance tests):
1) Summarize-Ticket-Concise:
  - Instruction: "Summarize the support ticket below into a single concise sentence, mentioning the customer impact, root cause (if clear), and a recommended next step."
  - Example input: transcript + ticket metadata
  - Expected output style: 1 sentence, <25 words, no PII, tag \"actionable\" or \"informational\"

2) Extract-Entities-For-Routing:
  - Instruction: "From the ticket text, extract customer product, platform version, error code, and priority. Respond as a JSON object with keys product, version, error_code, priority."
  - Important: model must output valid JSON only. Any non-JSON output is a hard failure.

3) Classify-Escalation-Need:
  - Instruction: "Classify whether the ticket requires escalation to Tier 2. Output one of: \"escalate\", \"no_escalation\". Brief justification (<=20 words)."

4) Generate-Prepop-Response:
  - Instruction: "Draft a short (2-3 sentence) response for the agent to send, in professional tone. Do not include any PII."

Private dataset subsets and test splits:
- Small holdout (smoke): 500 tickets randomly sampled across product lines (used for fast CI runs).
- Evaluation set: 5k tickets stratified by priority and product (used for acceptance thresholds).
- Regression archive: snapshots of monthly batches (12 months) retained for drift/regression checks.

Data preprocessing notes (applied by Redwood test harness):
- Agent names, phone numbers, emails replaced with <REDACTED> tokens except where tokenized IDs are permitted for internal mapping tests.
- Timestamp normalization to UTC.
- Ticket text truncated to 2048 tokens for consistency with model windows.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds (acceptance criteria):
1) Summarization fidelity:
  - ROUGE-L >= 0.56 on evaluation set AND human-rated accuracy >= 85% (sampled 200 items).
  - No hallucinated actionable next steps in >2% of samples (measured by human raters).

2) Extraction / routing (JSON entity extraction):
  - Exact match F1 for product and version >= 0.92.
  - Error code extraction precision >= 0.90.
  - Valid JSON outputs >= 99.0% (hard failure if <99%).

3) Escalation classifier:
  - Accuracy >= 90% on stratified evaluation set.
  - False negatives (tickets that needed escalation but predicted no_escalation) <= 6%.

4) Response quality (agent draft):
  - Human-rated helpfulness >= 4.0/5 on 300-sample eval.
  - No PII included (automatic PII detector must return zero positives on evaluation set).

5) Latency & cost:
  - P95 latency <= 450ms for summarize prompt on Dedicated config with batching profile B1.
  - Cost per 1k summarizations <= $4.00 token-equivalent (expected operating target).

6) Safety & privacy:
  - PII leakage rate: 0 confirmed leakages in holdout 5k set.
  - Model cannot output raw customer identifiers; any such occurrence triggers immediate rollback.

Acceptance gating rules (how metrics combine):
- All hard gates must pass: JSON validity >=99%, PII leakage 0, latency P95 <= 450ms.
- Soft gates: up to one soft metric (ROUGE, classifier accuracy, cost) may be marginally below target by <=3% but requires mitigation plan and product sign-off.

Automated test harness (how we run it):
- Smoke run (pre-commit): run pinned prompts on 500-sample smoke set, verify JSON validity and PII checks (<5 minutes).
- Full eval (pre-rollout): run across the 5k evaluation set with metric computation and store artifact in S3 under archives/evals/lumen/YYYYMMDD.
- Regression suite: nightly run against the last 3 snapshots; failure triggers alert to #applied-ml and creates JIRA-ML ticket.

Human evaluation protocol:
- Sample sizes: 200 summarization samples, 300 response drafts, 300 extraction items.
- Rater pool: mix of internal agents and 3 Lumen SMEs under NDA.
- Instructions and rubric stored at CONFLUENCE-1234.

Regression detection and rollback policy:
- Thresholds: if any primary metric drops >6% relative to last deployed snapshot AND human raters confirm decline, initiate escalation.
- Rollback: automated route to previous pinned model variant; SRE runbook in /sre/runbooks/rollbacks-md.

Deployment & routing considerations:
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor latency, error rates, metric drift.
- Fallback policy: if JSON-validity <99% or P95 latency >600ms for two consecutive 10-minute windows, route to model fallback vX-compat.

Security and compliance checkpoints:
- Verify VPC peering and least-privilege IAM roles before running Private evals.
- KMS/HSM key access verification required; record verification in linked_artifacts.
- Log redaction: ensure logs stored in EFK are masked per Lumen requirements.

Sign-off checklist (stakeholders must sign):
- Applied ML lead (Maya Patel): metric verification and regression plan acknowledged.
- Solutions Eng (Jordan Lee): integration and prompt fidelity confirmed.
- Security (Priya Nair): PII handling & KMS checks cleared.
- Lumen product owner (external): acceptance on UX quality and rollout plan.
- SRE: deployment/rollback tested in staging.

Post-signoff monitoring and maintenance:
- 30-day intensified monitoring window post-rollout with daily evaluation of key metrics.
- Monthly model quality report and quarterly re-eval with updated private data snapshot.

Open questions / risks:
- Edge-case long conversations where truncation may remove root-cause signals. Proposed mitigation: adaptive windowing for tickets flagged as high priority.
- SME availability for human ratings during tight release timelines.

Immediate next steps (for this doc iteration):
- Finalize evaluation split scripts and upload evaluation set to s3://redwood-evals/lumen/20241103 (action: Carlos Mendes).
- Run smoke harness and attach smoke report to JIRA-ML-778 (action: Maya Patel).
- Set up canary routing config in console and schedule 5% canary window (action: Jordan Lee).

Appendix: sample prompt examples and expected outputs:
- Summarize-Ticket-Concise (input): "User reports intermittent data drop on FiberPro v2.1 when uploading >50MB file, error code E402. Agent attempted restart, issue persists."
  Expected (ideal): "Data upload failures on FiberPro v2.1 (E402) causing user downtime; recommend escalate to platform team for storage node investigation. [actionable]"

- Extract-Entities-For-Routing (input): same as above
  Expected JSON: {"product":"FiberPro","version":"v2.1","error_code":"E402","priority":"high"}

Document history:
- 2024-11-03: Created by Maya Patel (initial draft)
- 2024-12-12: Added latency/cost targets and safety gates (Carlos Mendes)
- 2025-02-12: Updated sign-off checklist and regression policy after security review (Priya Nair)

Contact list:

- Jordan Lee (Solutions Eng) - jordan.lee@redwood.ai
- Priya Nair (Security) - priya.nair@redwood.ai

End of playbook.
